svg.title: Motion & graphs
svg.desc: Distance vs displacement: Distance: total path, scalar. Displacement: straight start-to-finish change with direction, vector. Round trip → zero displacement, nonzero distance. Average speed = total distance / total time. Useful estimates: Walking ≈ 1.5 m/s; running 3; cycling 6; sound in air 330. Conditions change values. s = vt at constant speed. Convert minutes to seconds and km to m before calculating. Velocity & acceleration: Velocity = speed with direction. Circle: constant speed can still mean changing velocity. a = (v−u)/t, m/s². 5 → 17 m/s in 4 s gives 3 m/s². Uniform acceleration: v²−u² = 2as only for constant a. From rest, a=2 over 25 m gives v=10 m/s. Free fall near Earth ≈ 9.8 m/s² when air resistance is negligible. Distance–time: Gradient = speed. Flat = rest; straight slope = constant speed. Curved graph: draw tangent at required time; gradient estimates instantaneous speed. Use a large gradient triangle. Velocity–time: Gradient = acceleration. Flat = constant velocity. Signed area = displacement; sum absolute areas for distance. Triangle + rectangle areas give movement. Count squares for a curved section if needed.
